html:
The Battle of Alcácer Quibir, called in Morocco the Battle of the Three Kings, was fought on 4 August 1578 near Ksar el-Kebir in northern Morocco. A Moroccan army crushed an invasion led by King Sebastian of Portugal.

Sebastian, young and eager for a crusade, came to back a deposed Saadi sultan against his uncle. All three kings died: Sebastian in the battle, the deposed sultan drowned, and the reigning sultan of illness. His brother Ahmad al-Mansur took the throne and grew rich on the ransoms of Portuguese nobles.

Sebastian left no heir, and in 1580 Philip II of Spain took the Portuguese crown, the Iberian Union. The victory gave the Saadi state great prestige in Europe and the Muslim world.
sum: The Battle of Alcácer Quibir, called in Morocco the Battle of the Three Kings, was fought on 4 August 1578 near Ksar el-Kebir in northern Morocco. A Moroccan army crushed an invasion led by King Sebastian of Portugal.
